title: Puerto Rico's oversight board strikes $35 billion restructuring deal with commonwealth's bondholders
主要内容: Puerto Rico's oversight board finalized a $35 billion restructuring deal with bondholders, offering over 60% average haircut, 36% on pre-2012 general obligation (GO) bonds, and 27% on public authority bonds. The agreement reduces outstanding Commonwealth-related bonds to less than $12 billion and cuts debt service by half to $21 billion over 30 years. Pre-2012 GO bonds receive 64 cents on the dollar, while 2012 and 2014 GO bonds receive 45 cents and 35 cents on the dollar, respectively. The board claims 2012 and 2014 bonds violated the constitution and are invalid. Bondholders may pursue pari recovery with pre-2012 bonds if they reject the settlement. Puerto Rico defaulted on general obligation bonds in July 2016 and has not made payments since. The restructuring, part of a larger $73 billion debt restructuring, includes $17 billion in sales tax-backed bonds and $4 billion in government development bank debt, with ongoing negotiations for $50 billion in pension liabilities. The plan, expected to be filed with the court within 30 days, faces opposition from the Government of Puerto Rico, which rejects pension cuts in the fiscal plan.
